newsitem.title: USA: Clinton meeting on Iraq ends.
newsitem.headline: Clinton meeting on Iraq ends.

text.p: President Clinton met in the Oval Office for 90 minutes on Friday night with top advisers on the sitution in Iraq and dispatched Defense Secretary William Perry to the region for consultations.

"They discussed the situation," said White House spokesman "and it was agreed that Defense Secretary Perry will depart tonight" on a trip that will include stops in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, as well as other nations.

Johnson declined to discuss what decisions were made at the White House session -- characterized as an update on developments in the showdown with Iraq. The United States has ordered a military buildup in the region, including the dispatching late on Friday of 5,000 Army troops to Kuwait.

Participants in the meeting included Perry, Vice President Al Gore, Secretary of State Warren Christopher, CIA Director John Deutsch, U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright, White House National Security Adviser Anthony Lake and Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff.

The United States has been saying it planned to retaliate against Iraq for attacks on allied aircraft patrols over no-fly zones in Iraq. Baghdad announced on Friday it would no longer attack planes in the no-fly zones, but Washington reacted with skepticism.
